Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the second innings to begin and we have around 90 minutes of play left for today. The two Umpires make their way out to the middle. Afghanistan fielders can be seen near the ropes and some players are warming up as well. Nishan Madushka and Dimuth Karunaratne are the two batters to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Nijat Masood has the new cherry in his hand and is all in readiness to commence the proceedings. Let's play...
... Second Innings ...

Right then, we still have more than an hour's play left on Day1 as the extra half hour will be used and this could be the best time for Afghanistan and their bowlers to make a mark. The Lankan openers will need to be watchful and make sure they remain unscathed as the pitch is great for batting and they can press home the advantage on Day 2. Let's see how Day 1 eventually pans out as Sri Lanka's reply is up next.

Sri Lanka will be very pleased to have bowled out the opposition on Day 1 itself but for about half of the day, they weren't up to the mark with the ball. Asitha Fernando gave them a solid start with a wicket in the first over but they couldn't quite build on it. Vishwa Fernando and Prabath Jayasuriya were able to pick up two quick wickets but Rahmat Shah stood strong. They bowled well in the second session, picking up three wickets in total but the crucial wicket of Shah in the latter part of that session was the turning point. Asitha Fernando ran through the tailenders after the Tea break and ended with three wickets so did Prabath Jayasuriya but it was Vishwa Fernando who picked up four wickets.

A fruitful first hour and ten minutes for Sri Lanka after the Tea break as they have reduced Afghanistan from 168/5 at the break to 198 all out. It was always going to be difficult for the visiting team once they lost Ikram Alikhil in the very first over after the interval but the lower-order batters managed to string a few more runs together and Qais Ahmad was the chief contributor with 21 runs. It was an up-and-down batting display overall with Rahmat Shah standing out and a couple of batters got in and got out which sot them dearly. They will now look to make early inroads late on Day 1 and come back on Day 2 with more intent.

The fielders also take their places on the field and it will be Vishwa Fernando who will start off proceedings with the ball after the break. Let's play...
... Day 1, Third Session ...

Rahmat Shah remained unfazed though and soon, Ikram Alikhil too started playing his shots and the two put on a steady stand worth 45 runs. Shah got into the 90s and looked in pole position to notch up a brilliant hundred but a clever piece of keeping by Sadeera Samarawickrama saw him get caught playing the paddle and Shah had to walk back for 91 well-made runs. Sri Lanka tried to force one more wicket before the session ended but Qais Ahmad showed good technique and along with Alikhil, saw his side safely into the break. Right then, Day 1 of this One-off Test match is well-poised and the final session will be crucial for both sides. Join us in about 15 minutes to see how Day 1 pans out.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the post-Lunch session to begin. The Umpires make their way out to the middle. The Sri Lankan fielders are seen in a huddle near the ropes for a quick chat before spreading out in the field. Rahmat Shah and Hashmatullah Shahidi stroll out to the middle and will resume their innings for Afghanistan. Prabath Jayasuriya will kick off the session with the ball for Sri Lanka. Let's play...
... Day 1, Second Session ...

As for Sri Lanka, Asitha Fernando provided the breakthrough in the very second ball of the match as he sent Ibrahim packing. Sri Lanka expected to climb on the top of the tourists after an early wicket but they were resisted pretty well by the Rahmat and Noor. Vishwa Fernando proved to be expensive. He conceded too many boundaries. Sri Lankan pacers also tried the short ball ploy and it was none other than Vishwa Fernando who dismissed the good-looking Noor Ali and tried to pull back the pace of scoring runs. Prabath Jayasuriya too, hasn't got much purchase off the deck as yet and the swing too, disappeared after the first half an hour or so. And now with the pitch getting better further under the sun to bat, their challenge will be to get quick wickets. Sri Lanka are also slow on the over rate which might penalize them ahead. The post-Lunch session will commence at 12:40 pm IST (7:10 am GMT). Stay tuned.

This brings up the end of the first session as the players head to Lunch on Day 1. It's been a mixed session with both teams starting off landing some punches in this session, but Afghanistan would be happy to have not lost many wickets and are cruising steadily at 90/2. Rahmat Shah and Noor Ali Zadran resisted the Sri Lankan pace attack after Ibrahim Zadran departed on a duck on the very second delivery of the match. Noor Ali Zadran, the debutant didn't at all look bothered and kept scoring runs quickly. Rahmat Shah equally been confident with his approach and these two mounted a strong counterattacking partnership of 57 runs and both of them were timing the ball well before Noor departed on a nothing shot on 31. He provided a strong platform for the other batters. Hashmatullah, the skipper is unbeaten with Rahmat. They have applied well and trusted their game and would aim to stitch a long partnership from here on in the next session.

A brace to end the first session! Full and outside off, Rahmat Shah gets on the front foot and opens the bat face to drive it away past the point region for a couple of runs. That will be Lunch on Day 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Sri Lanka. It will be the debutant Noor Ali Zadran to open the innings for Afghanistan alongside Ibrahim Zadran. Asitha Fernando has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Three slips and a gully in place. Let's go...

Right then, we are just a few minutes away from the start of the first-ever Test match between Sri Lanka and Afghanistan but first, it is time for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Afghanistan first, followed by Sri Lanka's national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof is pitchside. He says conditions are hot and humid here. He says that there's too much live grass on the deck and it is a pretty hard deck. The fast bowlers will get some movement and winning the toss and bowling first will be a good option. Adds that it will play well till the first three or four days.

The Afghan skipper, Hashmatullah Shahidi says that they wanted to bat first anyway and now will try to do their best with the bat. Adds that they have a lot of good players and the youngsters are doing well in first-class cricket. Mentions that they have four debutants with a couple of pacers and a left-arm spinner as well. Adds that Test cricket is the best format and they are excited as this game is a very good opportunity to showcase their talent in the longest format of the game.

Dhananjaya de Silva, the captain of Sri Lanka says that they will bowl first and are going with 3 seamers. He announces that one debutant Chamika Gunasekara is the squad who is a seamer. He says they haven't played much Test cricket so it is good to be playing here and also says that it's exciting to lead the side. Ends up saying that they hope for a good Test match.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Ibrahim Zadran, Noor Ali Zadran (On Test debut), Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Nasir Jamal, Ikram Alikhil (WK), Qais Ahmad (On Test debut), Zia ur Rehman (On Test debut), Mohammad Saleem, Naveed Zadran (On Test debut), Nijat Masood.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Dimuth Karunaratne, Nishan Madushka, Kusal Mendis, Angelo Mathews, Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya de Silva (C), Sadeera Samarawickrama (WK), Chamika Gunasekara (On Test debut), Prabath Jayasuriya, Vishwa Fernando, Asitha Fernando.
TOSS - Sri Lanka win the flip of the coin and they will BOWL first.

Afghanistan on the other hand are missing a few key players including their maestro Rashid Khan who continues to recover from his back injury but with the track not expected to a be rank turner like it has been in the past, it gives the Afghan pacers and opportunity to make their mark. A fascinating contest that looks to provide plenty of action over the course of the next few days. Can Sri Lanka notch up a home win? Or will Afghanistan pull off a shock defeat? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

Sri Lanka have a new Test skipper at the helm in the form of Dhananjaya de Silva and this game marks the start of a new era in Lankan cricket, one which they will hope to start on a positive note with a win and then build on it. They have some solid red-ball specialist batters in the side but the bowling does look a tinge weak that it usually is at home.
